The test image clearly shows:
1. A broken corn stalk
2. Numerous small black dots (pycnidia) scattered on the stalk rind surface
3. Tan/brown stalk color
4. Shredded pith visible at the break point

These are the hallmark features of Diplodia stalk rot - specifically the small black pycnidia on the lower internodes that cannot be easily scraped off. This distinguishes it from charcoal stalk rot (internal gray microsclerotia on vascular strands) and anthracnose stalk rot (shiny black rind discoloration).
